title: 8-round AES-256: Eight-round tradeoff: selected subkeys

target.description: Reduced 8-round AES-256 with whitening k_-1, final MixColumns omitted, and u_i=MC^-1(k_i). Returns k7 and selected u6, u5 and whitening bytes; the full k7 alone is128 bits of round-key material. This record stops at selected subkeys.

setting.key_relation: One fixed standard AES schedule; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: General fixed key; no weak-key subset is specified.
setting.plaintext_model: 2^(113+n) CP with2^-n retained special table. Source tradeoff parameters require fresh structures; n<=15 is a necessary128-bit-data constraint, not a proven admissible domain.
assumptions: The four-round one-byte differential is modeled at2^-120; Observation5 enumerates middle states using an average S-box count.
Wrong-key multisets are modeled random. The journal's separate probability proof has documented count/max-probability issues.
Reported time is the online stage; preprocessing is explicit and key-independent. Partial-encryption conversion factors are author estimates.
AES-256 saves only8 guessed bits in this construction.

success.description: No numerical finite-budget success is supplied for this exact partial_key_recovery endpoint. Expected right-pair counts, table coverage and wrong-key rejection are distinct from complete-output success. The existing Observation5 average-to-uniform enumeration conflict remains. Section6 keeps the original inner differential and2^113-data scale. The quoted2^24/2^32 per-pair key suggestions and optimized2^-8 table nonemptiness estimate are intermediate counts/models, not final success. The source shrinks the special table by2^n and increases data by2^n; that table fraction is not a proven hit probability or success curve.
